## Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- explain the relationship between image, container, volume, and network
- read a multi-stage Dockerfile
- diagnose service discovery and readiness in Compose
- preserve or remove local state intentionally

## Image and container lifecycle

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Source[Source code] --> Build[Image build]
    Build --> Image[Immutable image]
    Image --> Container[Running container]
    Container --> Logs[Logs]
    Container --> Volume[(Persistent volume)]
```

The image captures the application and runtime. Configuration and persistent
state enter at runtime.

## Multi-stage builds

A build stage compiles source with a complete toolchain. A runtime stage copies
only the required artifact and runtime dependencies.

Benefits include smaller images, fewer packages to patch, and a reproducible
build boundary. Pinning base-image versions remains necessary.

## Compose topology

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    Frontend[Angular and Nginx] --> Rental[Rental]
    Rental --> Auction[Auction]
    Rental --> Redis[(Redis)]
    Router[Event router] --> Redis
    Insurance[Insurance] --> Redis
    Rental --> Postgres[(PostgreSQL)]
    Insurance --> Postgres
```

Compose service names provide DNS names on the shared network. `localhost`
inside a container refers to that container.

## Startup and readiness

`depends_on` controls startup ordering only when combined with meaningful
health conditions. A running process may still reject traffic while it starts.

- Health checks describe container health.
- Application retries absorb short dependency delays.
- Readiness belongs to the service contract, not a fixed sleep duration.

## State and cleanup

Named volumes preserve Redis and PostgreSQL data across container replacement.

```bash
docker compose stop       # retain containers and volumes
docker compose down       # remove containers and network
docker compose down -v    # also remove named volumes
```

The final command destroys local data and requires deliberate use.

## Module investigation

1. List the Compose services, networks, and volumes.
2. Find every health check and dependency condition.
3. Explain why container hostnames differ from host-machine URLs.
4. Trace the Angular request through Nginx to a backend service.
